gap: The learner provides superficial evidence that is listed rather than thoroughly explained to support a complex argument.
instructions: When writing an argument, simply listing a brief point (e.g., 'a phone has a dictionary') is not enough. To persuade your reader, you must explain HOW and WHY your evidence supports your claim. Practice expanding basic points into fully developed, thoroughly explained evidence for a Grade 10 essay on cellphones in South African classrooms.
questions: Read this basic point: 'Cellphones give students access to online dictionaries, so they should be allowed.' Expand this into a fully developed paragraph (3-4 sentences) explaining HOW immediate dictionary access improves vocabulary, reading comprehension, and independent learning.

Read this basic point: 'Students can use news apps on phones for Social Sciences.' Expand this into a detailed explanation (3-4 sentences) describing HOW live news updates deepen critical thinking and real-world understanding in the classroom.

Read this basic point: 'Phones allow learners to record class lectures to study later.' Expand this into a thorough paragraph (3-4 sentences) explaining the educational benefit of audio recording for revision and addressing how it helps different learning styles.
answer_key: Allowing students to use digital dictionaries on smartphones significantly enhances real-time language acquisition. When learners encounter complex words during reading tasks, an online dictionary offers instant definitions, synonyms, and context examples without breaking their reading flow. This immediate support fosters independent learning skills and allows teachers to focus on higher-level comprehension rather than stopping to define individual words.

Integrating news apps on smartphones into Social Sciences lessons connects textbook concepts directly to current affairs. For instance, while learning about governance or environmental policy, students can access live news reports to analyze ongoing real-world events. This immediate connection encourages students to evaluate sources critically and participate in informed, meaningful classroom debates.

Using smartphones to record class lectures provides learners with a powerful tool for personalized revision. Students who struggle with fast-paced note-taking or who have auditory learning preferences can re-listen to complex explanations at home to solidify their understanding. Consequently, this practice reduces academic anxiety and ensures equal access to key instructional material for all student learning styles.
